title: Conductors and insulators
keyIdea: An electrical conductor is a material that lets electricity flow through it, so it completes a circuit and the bulb lights. An electrical insulator blocks the flow, so the bulb stays off. Metals such as copper, steel, iron and aluminium are good conductors; plastic, rubber, wood and glass are insulators. Shiny, hard or heavy is not the clue: test the material. Wires have a metal core to carry the electricity and a plastic coat to keep it off your hands.

kid: A bulb lights only when electricity can flow all the way round a loop, from the battery, through the bulb and back. Leave a gap and the flow stops. Put an object in the gap and you can test it.
If the bulb lights, the object is a conductor. It lets electricity through. If the bulb stays off, the object is an insulator. It blocks the flow.

Metals are good conductors. A steel paper clip, a coin, foil and an iron nail all light the bulb. Plastic, rubber and wood do not. A shiny plastic bead stays off, so shiny is not the clue. Ask: is it metal?

A wire has a copper core inside a plastic coat. The copper carries the electricity. The plastic is an insulator, so it keeps the electricity off your hands. Only test things with a small battery, never with a plug socket.
adult: This is a Year 4 topic in the national curriculum for England. Pupils should recognise some common conductors and insulators. They should also link metals with being good conductors. It builds on making a simple series circuit, where a bulb lights only in a complete loop. The same unit asks pupils to set up simple fair tests.

Metals conduct because some of their electrons are free to move. In plastic, rubber, dry wood and glass the electrons are held in place, so almost no current flows. The test circuit is a fair test: only the object in the gap changes. If a metal key lights the bulb, the cell and bulb work. So an object that leaves it dark is an insulator.

Common mistakes: thinking shiny means conductor, so a shiny plastic bead should work. Thinking hard or heavy things conduct. Thinking a wire conducts wherever you touch it, even on its plastic coat. Thinking the coat helps the current flow. Blaming a flat battery when the gap holds an insulator. Pencil lead (graphite) is a non-metal that conducts a little, so the bulb may glow dimly. Save it as an extra once the metal rule is secure.

In the lab learners close a gap with a steel key and test six everyday objects. They test a shiny plastic bead against a dull iron nail. They clip onto a wire's plastic coat, then onto its stripped copper end. Last, they pick conductors and insulators for a cable, a plug and a screwdriver.

familyTip: With a 1.5 V battery, a torch bulb and two wires with clips, test things from a drawer: a spoon, a key, a pencil, a lolly stick, foil, an eraser. Predict first, then test. Never test anything with a plug socket, which can kill.

visual.caption: Conductor or insulator? Drag each object, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: test objects in the gap of a circuit, sort conductors from insulators, see why shiny is not the clue and why wires have a coat.

practice.prompt: A steel spoon goes in the gap and the bulb lights. What is steel?
practice.hint: Did electricity get through the spoon to the bulb?
practice.explain: The bulb lit, so electricity flowed through the steel. Steel is a metal and a conductor.

practice.prompt: Ravi tests {n} objects. {k} of them light the bulb. How many objects are insulators?
practice.hint: Every object that did not light the bulb is an insulator. Take the conductors away from the total.
practice.explain: {n} objects take away {k} conductors leaves {=n-k} insulators.

practice.prompt: A box has {m} metal objects and {p} plastic objects. How many will light the bulb?
practice.hint: Which of the two materials is a conductor?
practice.explain: Metals conduct and plastic does not, so the {m} metal objects light the bulb.

practice.prompt: Why is the handle of an electrician's screwdriver made of rubber or plastic?
choices: They are insulators, so electricity cannot reach the hand
They are conductors, so electricity flows better
practice.hint: Which kind of material blocks electricity?
practice.explain: Rubber and plastic are insulators. They stop electricity flowing into the person holding the tool.

pool.prompt: A tray holds {a} coins, {b} wooden sticks and {d} rubber bands. How many objects are conductors?
pool.hint: Only one of these materials is a metal.
pool.explain: Coins are metal, so they conduct. Wood and rubber are insulators. That makes {a} conductors.

pool.prompt: A class tests {n} objects. {k} keep the bulb off. How many are conductors?
pool.hint: Objects that keep the bulb off are insulators. The rest are conductors.

pool.prompt: Which of these is an insulator?
pool.hint: Look for the one that is not a metal.
pool.explain: Plastic blocks electricity, so a plastic ruler is an insulator. The nail and the foil are metals and conduct.

pool.prompt: Zoe says a shiny plastic bead will light the bulb because it is shiny. Is she right?
choices: No, it is plastic, so it is an insulator
pool.hint: What is the bead made of?
pool.explain: Shiny is not the clue. The bead is plastic, which is an insulator, so the bulb stays off.

pool.prompt: A clip touches only the plastic coat of a wire. What happens?
pool.hint: Which part of the wire is the conductor: the coat or the core?
pool.explain: Only the copper core conducts. The plastic coat is an insulator, so no electricity flows and the bulb stays off.

pool.prompt: Most good conductors of electricity are…
pool.hint: Think about the paper clip, the coin and the foil. What do they have in common?
pool.explain: Metals are good conductors. Heavy or hard things, such as a stone or a wooden block, can still be insulators.

pool.prompt: A wooden stick keeps the bulb off. Sam says the battery is flat. How can he check?
choices: Put a metal key in the gap
pool.hint: Test with something you already know is a conductor.
pool.explain: If a metal key lights the bulb, the battery works. That shows the wood is an insulator.

pool.prompt: Why are cables made of copper inside and plastic outside?
choices: Copper carries the electricity and plastic keeps it off our hands
Plastic carries the electricity and copper makes it strong
pool.hint: Which one is the conductor and which is the insulator?
pool.explain: Copper is a metal conductor, so it carries the current. Plastic is an insulator, so it keeps people safe.
